/-!
# Hilbert's Fifth Problem

The actual formalization is in `FormalConjectures.HilbertProblems.«5»`.

Hilbert's fifth problem asks whether every locally Euclidean topological group admits a Lie group
structure. This was resolved affirmatively by Gleason, Montgomery, and Zippin in 1952.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_fifth_problem)
- [Gleason 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969548)
- [Montgomery–Zippin 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969549)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
-/

@[expose] public section

findings.description: The reference labelled “Gleason 1952” on line 31 links to DOI 10.2307/1969548, which identifies Iwasawa’s 1949 paper, not Gleason’s 1952 paper. This is a citation error; the mathematical summary remains correct.
findings.source_evidence: Crossref’s record at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2307/1969548 identifies Kenkichi Iwasawa, “On Some Types of Topological Groups,” Annals of Mathematics 50 (1949). Its title-and-author search identifies Andrew M. Gleason, “Groups Without Small Subgroups,” Annals of Mathematics 56 (1952), DOI 10.2307/1969795.

findings.description: The reference labelled “Montgomery–Zippin 1952” on line 32 links to DOI 10.2307/1969549, which identifies a 1949 paper by Følner, not the intended Montgomery–Zippin paper. This is a citation error, not a mathematical misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: Crossref’s record at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2307/1969549 identifies Erling Folner, “A Proof of the Main Theorem for Almost Periodic Functions in an Abelian Group,” Annals of Mathematics 50 (1949). Its title-and-author search identifies Deane Montgomery and Leo Zippin, “Small Subgroups of Finite-Dimensional Groups,” Annals of Mathematics 56 (1952), DOI 10.2307/1969796.

sources_consulted: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/ — especially Theorem 1 and Tao’s clarification that second countability is not assumed
Local Mathlib definitions: ChartedSpace, IsManifold, LieGroup, and ContinuousMulEquiv
review.notes: The requested file is a forwarding module with no mathematical declarations, answer slots, or category/formal_proof annotations of its own. Its summary agrees with Wikipedia and Tao’s Theorem 1. For context, I inspected the imported Hilbert5.hilbert_fifth_problem and its LieGroupPresentation definition, confirmed their elaborated types, and successfully compiled a scratch proof constructing a zero-dimensional presentation for every discrete group. The imported theorem’s research-solved status agrees with the sources. No mathematical misformalization was found in the requested file; the only findings are the two incorrect reference links. JSTOR and MathSciNet blocked access to the paper contents, so the bibliographic corrections were verified using Crossref records rather than the full papers. This is not a full review of every declaration in the imported HilbertProblems module.
